manifest.name: dsh-rtk-compressor
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin that routes bash commands through RTK (Rust Token Killer) to compress shell output and save context tokens.
manifest.author: sondin

bundle.text:
# Bundle patch layer: mounts dsh-rtk into the composed tree.
# The row loads this package's main entry as a plain Cordis plugin.
- insert:
    - id: rtk
      name: dsh-rtk
      config:
        enabled: true

readme.text:
[](https://github.com/sondin/dsh-rtk/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-rtk-compressor)
[](LICENSE)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that
routes eligible `bash` commands through **RTK (Rust Token Killer)** so the output
an agent reads back is already filtered, grouped, truncated, and deduplicated —
saving context tokens the same way RTK's own agent hooks do.

- Zero prompt changes: the `bash` tool keeps working, but commands like
  `git status`, `cat src/main.rs`, `grep -rn TODO src`, `npm test`, `git diff`,
  and `find . -name '*.ts'` are transparently rewritten to their `rtk`
  equivalents (`rtk git status`, `rtk read src/main.rs`, `rtk grep ...`,
  `rtk cargo test`, ...) before execution.
- Fail-open: if RTK is not installed, times out, has no equivalent for a
  command, or a deny rule matches, the original command runs unchanged.
- An `rtk` skill is registered for the agent, teaching it how to interpret
  compressed output, recall elided content (`rtk recall`), bypass filtering
  (`rtk bypass`), and read savings analytics (`rtk gain`).

DSH's tool pipeline deliberately cannot rewrite `exec.arguments` (`tools/pre-execute`
and `tools/execute` receive deep-frozen arguments). Instead, this plugin wraps the
**shell executor seam**: the `bash` tool resolves a `ShellExecSpec` through
`ctx.shell.resolve(...)` and spawns with `ctx.shell.execute(spec)`. The plugin
wraps `ctx.shell.execute` and, for each command, calls `rtk rewrite <command>`
(RTK's own "single source of truth" hook command):

| `rtk rewrite` exit | meaning | plugin behavior |
|---|---|---|
| 0 / 3 | rewrite printed | executes the rewritten `rtk ...` command |
| 1 | no RTK equivalent | passes the command through unchanged |
| 2 | deny rule matched | passes through (DSH's own approval already ran) |
| spawn error / timeout | RTK unavailable | passes through; failure is not cached |

The rewritten command runs with `RTK_SUPPRESS_HOOK_WARNING=1` so RTK's
"install a hook" nag never pollutes tool output. A bounded LRU cache avoids
re-spawning `rtk rewrite` for repeated commands.

Sandboxing is unaffected: the sandbox executor still applies the configured
sandbox mode to the spawned process, and RTK preserves exit codes, so the
`[exit code: N]` markers stay accurate.

The plugin is a DSH bundle (an npm package whose `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch`). Install it into a profile with the plugin manager:

- **Web UI**: open the **Plugins** page in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar and
  install the bundle by spec (registry name `dsh-rtk-compressor`, git URL
  `https://github.com/sondin/dsh-rtk`, or a local
  `link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-rtk`).
- **`plugin_manager` tool**: call `installBundle` with the same spec.
- **CLI** (when available): `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <spec>` then
  enable the `dsh-rtk` bundle.

The bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` mounts the plugin row:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: rtk
      name: dsh-rtk
      config:

After installation, restart DSH (or rely on HMR when the profile runs with
live patch reload). The plugin takes effect for every `bash` tool call.

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | master switch; when `false` every command passes through |
| `binary` | string | `"rtk"` | path to the RTK binary |
| `timeoutMs` | number | `2000` | per-`rtk rewrite` call timeout |
| `cacheSize` | number | `256` | LRU cache size for rewrite results |
| `excludedCommands` | string[] | `[]` | command prefixes that are never rewritten |
| `debug` | boolean | `false` | log each rewrite decision to the harness logger |

Example:

```yaml
- id: rtk
  name: dsh-rtk
  config:
    enabled: true

When the `skills` service is present (it is in the default composition), the
plugin registers a runtime skill named `rtk`. The skill tells the agent:

- bash output may be compressed; exit codes remain accurate
- use `rtk recall <hash>` / `rtk recall --grep <pattern>` to recover elided content
- use `rtk bypass <command>` to execute a command without filtering
- use `rtk gain`, `rtk discover`, `rtk session` for savings analytics

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm test
```

Tests cover the rewrite decision logic (with a fake shell executor), the disposer
restoring the original executor on plugin unload, and the real `rtk rewrite`
CLI behavior (rewrites, chains, no-equivalent, already-rtk commands).

- [DeepTrial/dsh-bash-rtk](https://github.com/DeepTrial/dsh-bash-rtk) — a
  TypeScript implementation of the same idea (subclassing the official DSH
  executors with a whitelist-based rewrite). This project differs by rewriting
  **command chains** (`a && b`), using RTK's own `rtk rewrite` as the source of
  truth (so new RTK commands work without plugin updates), registering an `rtk`
  skill for agents, and requiring **no build step**.
- [rtk](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) — the Rust Token Killer CLI this plugin
  routes commands through.
